paper_metadata.title: The Qubit Shift: Unveiling Next-Generation Deep Learning with Quantum Computing
paper_metadata.venue: 2025 10th International Conference on Information Technology Trends (ITT), IEEE

summary: Survey-style paper proposing a hybrid quantum-classical deep learning architecture with parametrised rotation gates on variational quantum circuits for feature encoding. No finance-specific experimental results are reported: Table 1 lists an S&P 500 dataset with 6-qubit amplitude encoding but no accuracy / loss numbers for it. Headline benchmarks are image classification on MNIST (98.7% test accuracy with 1,250 parameters vs. 97.8% / 25,000 parameters classically) and a 47% reduction in training time across datasets.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical deep network with parametrised rotation gates for feature encoding; benchmarked primarily on MNIST image classification (NON-FINANCE) and intended for transfer to an S&P 500 regression task that is not quantitatively reported.

algorithm.variant: hybrid quantum-classical neural network with variational quantum circuits in feature encoding layer
algorithm.ansatz: parametrised rotation gates (R_x, R_y, R_z) with staged classical-then-quantum training

hyperparameters.training_strategy: staged: classical layers first (quantum frozen), then joint training with reduced learning rate

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Amplitude encoding for MNIST (10 qubits) and S&P 500 regression (6 qubits); angle encoding for CIFAR-10 (12 qubits); hybrid for QM9 (8 qubits).

problem_instance.dataset_name: MNIST (headline result); S&P 500 (listed but no finance numerics reported)

dataset_specification.description: MNIST: 70,000 samples, 784 features, 10 classes, amplitude encoding, 10 qubits. S&P 500: 100,000 samples, 50 features, regression, amplitude encoding, 6 qubits -- listed in Table 1 but no accuracy or loss values provided.

results.notes: MNIST test accuracy for the hybrid quantum-classical model (Sec. IV.C). NOT a finance benchmark.
Reported 47% average training-time reduction across datasets vs. classical baseline (conflicts with abstract, which states training is '47 times as long'; treated as a typo in the abstract).

classical_baselines.notes: Classical NN with ~25,000 parameters vs. 1,250 parameters for hybrid model (Sec. IV.C).
classical_baselines.method_name: Classical neural network of comparable architecture

speedup_claims.notes: Claim limited to image classification; no quantitative finance benchmark is reported despite S&P 500 being listed as a target dataset.

notes: Paper is vague on hardware and noise; numbers read from Table 1 and Sec. IV.C.
